page: Amazon Web Services x8i.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. Running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, the server is equipped with a dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor delivering 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores with two threads per core at a 3.9 GHz clock speed. The processor architecture includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large shared 480 MB L3 cache. It also supports instruction extensions including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, enabling accelerated vector processing and matrix operations.

Memory configuration is the central focus of the x8i.4xlarge, incorporating 256 GB of DDR5 RAM clocked at 7 GHz. This yields an expansive allocation of 16 GB of memory per vCPU, accommodating large working sets directly in memory. In terms of peripheral hardware, the server includes no local bundled storage, requiring persistent data to reside on external network-attached volumes. It provides a baseline network throughput of 8 Gbps and contains zero discrete GPU accelerators, keeping the system resources concentrated on memory density and central compute.

Benchmark data reflects strong execution in single-core and memory-centric operations. In Geekbench testing, the server achieves strong single-core scores alongside top-tier text processing throughput. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also show strong performance, while multi-core compute across stress-ng and PassMark settles within average ranges typical for an 8-core allocation. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 127.98 GB/s and write bandwidth achieves 62.97 GB/s, supporting substantial in-memory operations such as Redis SET rates exceeding 30 million operations per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the x8i.4xlarge prioritizes memory capacity over massive raw CPU scale, allowing organizations to avoid overpaying for unnecessary vCPUs when scaling memory-heavy services. The lack of integrated NVMe drives presents an operational tradeoff, requiring network bandwidth to handle primary storage I/O. Consequently, the instance is best suited for in-memory databases, distributed key-value stores, real-time caching tiers, and memory-heavy data transformation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services x8i.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor. Configured with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores running at 3.9 GHz with a 480 MB L3 cache, the system features 256 GB of DDR5 memory, delivering 16 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware support for Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions facilitates acceleration in text processing, decompression, and lightweight inference. Network throughput provides an 8 Gbps baseline, and the instance includes no bundled local storage, relying on network volumes. Benchmarks demonstrate solid single-thread compute capabilities alongside high memory bandwidth. The server provides strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound environments where high RAM-to-CPU ratios are necessary without paying for unneeded compute density, making it a targeted fit for in-memory databases, Redis deployments, data analytics, and large enterprise caching layers.
